lines.text: The last time these two met at a World Cup, England scored six. It was 2018, and Panama's first ever World Cup became a painful lesson in the gap between football's powers and those still learning the ropes.
But before the first whistle, a question hangs in the air. A single afternoon once told the world who Panama were. Some things cannot be erased. Hold on to that.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode seventy. England, versus Panama. Group L. The rematch.
Eight years later, Panama return — with a point to prove and a memory to exorcise. And this is not the same Panama.
England — the Three Lions. White and red, and the weight that always follows them, the favourites who scored six the last time and are expected to do it again.
Harry Kane wears the armband like a man whose time is running out. Jude Bellingham, the Galáctico. Phil Foden, pure imagination. Declan Rice, the anchor. Bukayo Saka, electric on the wing.
But the eighth anniversary of that six-one hangs over everything. Panama's players have spoken of it all week — not with anger, but with a quiet determination to show how far they have come.
Panama — La Marea Roja. The red tide, no longer the team the world wrote off in a single scoreline, carried now by players who have made it to Europe and the very top.
Carrasquilla conducts the midfield. Edgar Bárcenas, El Mago, conjures chances from nothing. Murillo flies from full-back. And Waterman waits for the goal that defines a career.
So here it is. The ghost of twenty-eighteen against a nation that refuses to be defined by it. Kane's class, against El Mago's spell.
And one duel decides the night — Harry Kane, the closer who never wastes a chance, against Edgar Bárcenas, the magician who only needs one moment to rewrite a story.
And before the shot that almost changes everything — stay with me. Because first, Panama strike a blow eight years in the making.
Here is how we see it. The favourites get a shock. And a small nation announces it is not who it used to be.
Cecilio Waterman pounces and smashes it past Pickford. Panama, one — England, nil. The goal of a lifetime, against the team that once scored six.
And it almost gets better. Forty-third minute, Bárcenas receives on the left, cuts inside — a feint, a shuffle, a burst — and Rice is left grasping at air.
The shot curls toward the far post — and flies inches wide. Bárcenas looks to the sky. Some moments are perfect in every way but the ending.
England answer. Around the hour, Kane does what Kane does — half a yard, one touch, the equalizer. One — one. The favourites breathe again.
But Panama do not fold. They defend every blade of grass, and the team that lost six-one walks off level with England. The red tide holds.
A shock goal. A shot inches wide. An equalizer from a captain under pressure. A memory eight years deep, and a small nation standing tall against it.
Our prediction — England one, Panama one. A level scoreline. Not played yet — the real ninety minutes are yours to watch.
Because this match was about more than revenge. It is about a small nation refusing to be defined, forever, by one painful afternoon in Russia.
Tonight, Panama did not erase twenty-eighteen. They did something harder — they made the world stop talking about it.
Do you agree? Comment ENGLAND if the favourites escape. Comment PANAMÁ if the red tide finally laid the ghost to rest.

What cannot be erased. On the islands of Panama, the Guna make the mola — cloth stitched in layer upon layer, where you never unpick the past, you sew a new story over it. That is how a people refuse to be erased. Legend seventy. The Mola Maker. The keeper of the layered story.
The players carry the fight. The Mola Maker carries the truth — you cannot erase a past, only outgrow it. This Legend is yours to claim and collect.

Then pick three of the forty-eight nations, and every goal they score, scores for you. Free to play, just for fun. No prizes — only glory.
